courses.title: Complete Clutch Essentials
moduleTitles: Dual Mass Flywheel Design and Operation

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the clutch in a manual transmission vehicle?
questions.explanation: The clutch connects/disconnects engine drive for starting, stopping, and gear changes.

options.label: A
options.body: To increase engine power at high speed

options.label: B
options.body: To connect and disconnect engine drive to the transmission so gears can be changed and the vehicle can stop with the engine running

options.label: C
options.body: To cool the transmission oil

options.label: D
options.body: To charge the battery while driving

questions.prompt: In a typical single-plate clutch, the friction disc is splined to which part and clamped between which two parts?
questions.explanation: The disc drives the input shaft and is clamped between flywheel and pressure plate.

options.label: A
options.body: The crankshaft; the gearbox casing and bell housing

options.label: B
options.body: The transmission input shaft; the flywheel and the pressure plate

options.label: C
options.body: The driveshaft; the differential and axle

options.label: D
options.body: The release bearing; the pedal and cable

questions.prompt: What does a diaphragm spring in the pressure plate do when the clutch pedal is pressed?
questions.explanation: Pressing the pedal moves the diaphragm fingers and lifts clamping load to release the disc.

options.label: A
options.body: It clamps the disc harder to the flywheel

options.label: B
options.body: Its fingers are pushed in, pulling the pressure plate away so the disc is released

options.label: C
options.body: It locks the differential

options.label: D
options.body: It pumps hydraulic fluid to the brakes

questions.prompt: Why use a multi-plate clutch instead of a single-plate clutch?
questions.explanation: Stacked plates multiply friction surfaces, giving high torque capacity in a small diameter.

options.label: A
options.body: It needs no release bearing

options.label: B
options.body: More friction surfaces transmit more torque in a compact size

options.label: C
options.body: It eliminates the flywheel

options.label: D
options.body: It works without any friction material

questions.prompt: A wet multi-plate clutch differs from a dry multi-plate clutch because it:
questions.explanation: Wet clutches run in oil for cooling and durability; dry clutches run in air.

options.label: A
options.body: Runs in oil, which cools the plates and gives smoother, longer-lasting engagement

options.label: B
options.body: Has no plates at all

options.label: C
options.body: Only works on electric vehicles

options.label: D
options.body: Uses air pressure to clamp the plates

questions.prompt: What is the main job of a dual mass flywheel (DMF)?
questions.moduleTitle: Dual Mass Flywheel Design and Operation
questions.explanation: The DMF damps crankshaft torsional pulses, reducing gearbox rattle and vibration.

options.label: A
options.body: To increase top speed

options.label: B
options.body: To absorb and damp engine torsional vibration before it reaches the gearbox

options.label: C
options.body: To double the clutch clamping force

options.label: D
options.body: To replace the starter motor

questions.prompt: Inside a DMF, the primary and secondary masses are connected by:
questions.moduleTitle: Dual Mass Flywheel Design and Operation
questions.explanation: Arc springs between the two masses allow movement that absorbs vibration.

options.label: A
options.body: A rigid solid bolted joint with no movement

options.label: B
options.body: Arc springs that allow controlled relative movement between the masses

options.label: C
options.body: A rubber drive belt

options.label: D
options.body: Hydraulic fluid only

questions.prompt: Which symptom most points to a worn or failing DMF?
questions.moduleTitle: Dual Mass Flywheel Design and Operation
questions.explanation: Idle and start/stop rattle plus vibration are classic DMF failure symptoms.

options.label: A
options.body: A flat tire vibration at motorway speed only

options.label: B
options.body: Rattle or knocking at idle and on start-up/shut-down, with vibration through the vehicle

options.label: C
options.body: The headlights flickering

options.label: D
options.body: Low engine oil pressure

questions.prompt: A clutch is slipping. Which test result confirms slip?
questions.explanation: Rising RPM without matching road speed under load confirms the disc is slipping.

options.label: A
options.body: Engine RPM rises under load in a high gear but road speed does not rise with it

options.label: B
options.body: The pedal feels very heavy

options.label: C
options.body: First gear is hard to select at a standstill

options.label: D
options.body: The release bearing is noisy with the pedal up

questions.prompt: A clutch drags (does not fully release), often due to air in the hydraulic system or incorrect adjustment. The driver will most likely report:
questions.explanation: Incomplete release keeps the input shaft turning, making first/reverse selection hard.

options.label: A
options.body: Difficulty selecting first and reverse gear, with crunching

options.label: B
options.body: The engine overheating

options.label: C
options.body: A slipping clutch smell at high speed

options.label: D
options.body: Loss of power steering

questions.prompt: Why does a vehicle need different gear ratios?
questions.explanation: Low gears multiply torque to pull away; high gears suit cruising speed.

options.label: A
options.body: To keep the radio tuned to different stations

options.label: B
options.body: To multiply engine torque for pulling away and allow higher road speed with lower engine load as speed rises

options.label: C
options.body: To change the direction of the exhaust

options.label: D
options.body: To recharge the gearbox oil

questions.prompt: In a constant-mesh manual gearbox, the gear pairs are:
questions.explanation: Constant-mesh gears stay meshed; a sliding hub locks the chosen gear to its shaft.

options.label: A
options.body: Only meshed when the driver moves the gear lever

options.label: B
options.body: Always in mesh; drive is locked in by dog teeth / synchromesh hubs sliding onto the selected gear

options.label: C
options.body: Driven by a rubber belt

options.label: D
options.body: Connected by a chain only in reverse

questions.prompt: What does the synchromesh (synchronizer) do during a gear change?
questions.explanation: Synchromesh matches speeds by friction first, so engagement is smooth and quiet.

options.label: A
options.body: It cools the gear oil

options.label: B
options.body: It uses friction to match the speed of the gear and shaft before the dog teeth engage, preventing crunching

options.label: C
options.body: It locks both axles together

options.label: D
options.body: It measures road speed

questions.prompt: How is reverse gear usually obtained in a manual gearbox?
questions.explanation: A reverse idler reverses output direction without reversing the engine.

options.label: A
options.body: By reversing engine rotation

options.label: B
options.body: By adding an idler gear that reverses the direction of the output shaft

options.label: C
options.body: By turning the steering wheel fully

options.label: D
options.body: By switching the clutch off

questions.prompt: Worn synchromesh on second gear will most likely cause:
questions.explanation: Worn synchro rings cannot match speeds in time, so second gear crunches.

options.label: A
options.body: Crunching when changing into second gear, especially when rushed or cold

options.label: B
options.body: The clutch to slip in fifth gear

options.label: C
options.body: Loss of reverse gear only

options.label: D
options.body: The speedometer to stop working

questions.prompt: A transaxle differs from a separate transmission and final drive because it:
questions.explanation: A transaxle packages gearbox, final drive, and differential together in one casing.

options.label: A
options.body: Has no gears at all

options.label: B
options.body: Combines the gearbox, final drive, and differential in one housing

options.label: C
options.body: Is only used on rear-wheel-drive trucks

options.label: D
options.body: Uses no lubricant

questions.prompt: Manual transaxles are most commonly used on:
questions.explanation: Transaxles suit front-wheel drive, keeping the powertrain compact at the driven end.

options.label: A
options.body: Front-wheel-drive cars, where the engine and driven wheels are at the same end

options.label: B
options.body: Steam locomotives

options.label: C
options.body: Aircraft

options.label: D
options.body: Rear-engine buses only

questions.prompt: In a front-wheel-drive transaxle, power leaves the differential to the wheels through:
questions.explanation: Half shafts with CV joints carry drive from the transaxle differential to the front wheels.

options.label: A
options.body: A long propshaft to the rear axle

options.label: B
options.body: Drive shafts (half shafts) with constant velocity joints

options.label: C
options.body: A chain drive to each wheel

options.label: D
options.body: The steering rack

questions.prompt: Why must the correct specified oil be used in a manual transaxle?
questions.explanation: Shared gear/diff oil must suit synchro friction and gear protection — wrong oil causes shift problems.

options.label: A
options.body: The same oil often lubricates both the gears and the differential, and the wrong grade/additives can harm synchromesh and bearings

options.label: B
options.body: Oil type makes no difference in any gearbox

options.label: C
options.body: To change the colour of the casing

options.label: D
options.body: Only automatic transmissions need oil

questions.prompt: A transaxle whines in all gears and the noise changes with road speed, not engine speed in a single gear. This most likely points to:
questions.explanation: Noise tied to road speed across gears points to the final drive/differential side.

options.label: A
options.body: Worn clutch release bearing

options.label: B
options.body: Final drive / differential or wheel-side components in the transaxle

options.label: C
options.body: A slipping drive belt

options.label: D
options.body: Low coolant level

questions.prompt: A dual clutch transmission (DCT) is best described as:
questions.explanation: A DCT splits odd and even gears between two clutches/sub-transmissions.

options.label: A
options.body: An automatic with only one clutch and a torque converter

options.label: B
options.body: Two manual sub-transmissions in one unit, one for odd gears and one for even gears, each with its own clutch

options.label: C
options.body: A CVT with a belt and pulleys

options.label: D
options.body: A manual gearbox with no clutches

questions.prompt: How does a DCT achieve such fast gear changes?
questions.explanation: Preselection plus a clutch-to-clutch swap gives very fast shifts.

options.label: A
options.body: The driver changes gear twice as fast

options.label: B
options.body: The next gear is preselected on the other sub-transmission, so the change is a swap of clutches

options.label: C
options.body: It skips every second gear

options.label: D
options.body: It turns the engine off during the shift

questions.prompt: In a DCT, while first gear is driving through clutch 1, the control system will normally:
questions.explanation: The idle sub-transmission preselects the likely next gear.

options.label: A
options.body: Leave all other gears disengaged

options.label: B
options.body: Preselect second gear on the other sub-transmission ready for the upshift

options.label: C
options.body: Preselect reverse gear

options.label: D
options.body: Disconnect the engine completely

questions.prompt: A wet-clutch DCT differs from a dry-clutch DCT because the wet type:
questions.explanation: Oil-cooled wet clutches suit higher torque/heat; dry clutches are simpler and more efficient.

options.label: A
options.body: Cannot be used in cars

options.label: B
options.body: Runs its clutches in oil, handling higher torque and heat better, at some cost to efficiency

options.label: C
options.body: Has no mechatronics unit

options.label: D
options.body: Only has two gears

questions.prompt: What is the mechatronics unit in a DCT?
questions.explanation: Mechatronics combines valves, actuators, sensors, and control electronics for the DCT.

options.label: A
options.body: The driver's gear lever

options.label: B
options.body: The combined hydraulic/electronic control unit that operates the clutches and shift actuators from TCM commands

options.label: C
options.body: A second engine

options.label: D
options.body: The parking brake module

questions.prompt: Why can a DCT feel hesitant or jerky at very low speed and in stop-start traffic?
questions.explanation: Creeping slips a clutch; sustained creep overheats it, so protection strategies intervene.

options.label: A
options.body: It has no first gear

options.label: B
options.body: Clutches are being slipped to creep like a torque converter, and repeated low-speed slipping builds heat

options.label: C
options.body: The belt stretches at low speed

options.label: D
options.body: It only works above 30 mph

questions.prompt: What does DCT clutch overheating protection most likely do?
questions.explanation: Thermal protection warns and reduces slip/drive until the clutches cool.

options.label: A
options.body: Turns off the headlights

options.label: B
options.body: Warns the driver and may limit clutch slip, change shift strategy, or disengage drive until temperatures fall

options.label: C
options.body: Increases clutch slip deliberately

options.label: D
options.body: Locks the steering

questions.prompt: Compared with a conventional torque-converter automatic, a DCT generally offers:
questions.explanation: Direct mechanical drive and clutch-swap shifts give DCTs speed and efficiency.

options.label: A
options.body: Slower shifts and higher fuel use

options.label: B
options.body: Fast shifts and good efficiency because there is a direct mechanical connection, with no torque converter slip in normal driving

options.label: C
options.body: No gear changes at all

options.label: D
options.body: Unlimited creep with no wear

questions.prompt: A DCT will not engage drive and stores clutch actuator faults. The best first checks are:
questions.explanation: Fluid, power/grounds, and clutch position/temperature scan data lead DCT diagnosis.

options.label: A
options.body: Tire pressures and wheel alignment

options.label: B
options.body: DCT fluid level/condition, mechatronics supply and grounds, and scan data for clutch position/temperature

options.label: C
options.body: Engine coolant colour only

options.label: D
options.body: The radio fuse

questions.prompt: Why is the specified DCT fluid and service interval especially important?
questions.explanation: DCT fluid serves clutches and hydraulics; wrong/degraded fluid harms control and shift feel.

options.label: A
options.body: The same fluid may cool/lubricate clutches and operate the mechatronics, so wrong or degraded fluid affects shift quality and clutch control

options.label: B
options.body: Fluid never affects a DCT

options.label: C
options.body: Any engine oil works the same

options.label: D
options.body: DCTs are sealed and contain no fluid

questions.prompt: In a conventional automatic transmission, gear changes are made by:
questions.explanation: Automatics shift by applying/releasing friction elements on planetary members.

options.label: A
options.body: The driver sliding gears along a shaft by hand

options.label: B
options.body: Applying and releasing clutches and brakes (bands/multi-plate packs) to change which planetary members are held or driven

options.label: C
options.body: Moving a belt between pulleys

options.label: D
options.body: Turning the torque converter around

questions.prompt: What does the 'P' (Park) position engage that the other positions do not?
questions.explanation: Park adds a pawl locking the output; other ranges are hydraulic/electronic selections.

options.label: A
options.body: The torque converter lock-up clutch

options.label: B
options.body: A parking pawl that mechanically locks the output shaft

options.label: C
options.body: The highest gear

options.label: D
options.body: The radiator fan

questions.prompt: The three main elements inside a torque converter are:
questions.explanation: Impeller, turbine, and stator are the converter's three main elements.

options.label: A
options.body: Ring gear, planet gears, and carrier

options.label: B
options.body: Impeller (pump), turbine, and stator

options.label: C
options.body: Rotor, stator, and brushes

options.label: D
options.body: Input shaft, layshaft, and mainshaft

questions.prompt: What does the stator do at low speed / high slip in a torque converter?
questions.explanation: At high slip the stator redirects flow to multiply torque; it freewheels near coupling speed.

options.label: A
options.body: It disconnects the engine

options.label: B
options.body: It redirects fluid returning from the turbine so the converter multiplies torque

options.label: C
options.body: It locks the converter solid

options.label: D
options.body: It cools the fluid in the radiator

questions.prompt: A simple planetary gear set consists of:
questions.explanation: Sun, planets/carrier, and ring gear make up a simple planetary set.

options.label: A
options.body: Two bevel gears and a cross pin

options.label: B
options.body: A sun gear, planet gears on a carrier, and an outer ring (annulus) gear

options.label: C
options.body: A worm and a wheel

options.label: D
options.body: A chain and two sprockets

questions.prompt: In a planetary set, different ratios (including reverse and overdrive) are obtained by:
questions.explanation: Holding/driving different members gives reduction, direct drive, overdrive, or reverse.

options.label: A
options.body: Changing the size of the gears while driving

options.label: B
options.body: Holding one member, driving another, and taking output from the third in different combinations

options.label: C
options.body: Adding more fluid

options.label: D
options.body: Reversing the engine

questions.prompt: What is the main role of the hydraulic system and valve body in a conventional automatic?
questions.explanation: The valve body routes line pressure to friction elements and controls shift quality.

options.label: A
options.body: To steer the vehicle

options.label: B
options.body: To direct pressurised fluid to apply/release the correct clutches and brakes for each gear, and to control shift pressure and feel

options.label: C
options.body: To pump fuel to the engine

options.label: D
options.body: To operate the windshield wipers

questions.prompt: Line pressure that is too low will most likely cause:
questions.explanation: Low line pressure cannot clamp friction elements firmly, so they slip and wear.

options.label: A
options.body: Harsh, violent shifts only

options.label: B
options.body: Clutch/band slip, delayed or flared shifts, and rapid friction wear

options.label: C
options.body: The engine to stall at idle every time

options.label: D
options.body: Loss of brake pressure

questions.prompt: Why must the exact specified ATF be used?
questions.explanation: ATF friction/viscosity specs are matched to the clutches and controls of each unit.

options.label: A
options.body: All ATF is identical, so it does not matter

options.label: B
options.body: Friction characteristics, viscosity, and additives differ; the wrong ATF can cause shudder, harsh or slipping shifts, and damage

options.label: C
options.body: Only the colour matters

options.label: D
options.body: ATF is the same as engine oil

questions.prompt: The transmission control module (TCM) decides shift points mainly from inputs such as:
questions.explanation: Load, speed, temperatures, and demand drive the TCM shift schedule and pressure control.

options.label: A
options.body: Radio volume and seat position

options.label: B
options.body: Engine load/throttle, vehicle speed, engine and fluid temperatures, and driver demand

options.label: C
options.body: Tire tread depth only

options.label: D
options.body: Windshield washer level

questions.prompt: A continuously variable transmission (CVT) differs from a stepped automatic because it:
questions.explanation: A CVT varies ratio continuously instead of stepping through fixed gears.

options.label: A
options.body: Has only neutral and reverse

options.label: B
options.body: Provides a seamless range of ratios with no fixed gear steps

options.label: C
options.body: Uses a manual clutch pedal

options.label: D
options.body: Has exactly three forward gears

questions.prompt: In the most common automotive CVT, ratio is changed by:
questions.explanation: Variable pulleys change effective diameter to vary the ratio seamlessly.

options.label: A
options.body: Sliding gears along a splined shaft

options.label: B
options.body: Moving the sides of two variable-diameter pulleys so the belt/chain rides higher on one and lower on the other

options.label: C
options.body: Switching planetary members on and off

options.label: D
options.body: Changing tire size while driving

questions.prompt: The drive element between the CVT pulleys is usually:
questions.explanation: Car CVTs use a steel push belt or chain matched to the pulley design.

options.label: A
options.body: A multi-plate clutch pack

options.label: B
options.body: A steel push belt or a chain designed for the pulleys

options.label: C
options.body: A rubber V-belt like an accessory drive belt on most car CVTs

options.label: D
options.body: A set of bevel gears

questions.prompt: Why does a CVT improve fuel economy in normal driving?
questions.explanation: Continuous ratios keep the engine near its efficient operating point.

options.label: A
options.body: It removes the engine from the car

options.label: B
options.body: It lets the engine stay near its most efficient speed for the load instead of being tied to fixed gear steps

options.label: C
options.body: It turns the engine off at all speeds

options.label: D
options.body: It makes the vehicle lighter

questions.prompt: Many CVTs use a torque converter or start clutch at low speed mainly to:
questions.explanation: A converter/start clutch gives smooth launch and creep before the belt drive takes over.

options.label: A
options.body: Provide smooth pull-away and creep, and isolate vibration at a standstill

options.label: B
options.body: Lock the differential

options.label: C
options.body: Charge the battery

options.label: D
options.body: Cool the belt

questions.prompt: Why is the specified CVT fluid critical and not interchangeable with regular ATF?
questions.explanation: Belt/pulley friction is controlled by the fluid — wrong fluid causes slip and scoring.

options.label: A
options.body: CVT fluid is only a different colour

options.label: B
options.body: It must provide the exact metal-to-metal friction between belt/chain and pulleys plus hydraulic control; wrong fluid can cause belt slip and pulley damage

options.label: C
options.body: CVTs contain no fluid

options.label: D
options.body: Any gear oil gives the same result

questions.prompt: A CVT vehicle shudders on pull-away and the fluid is dark and burnt-smelling. The most likely concern is:
questions.explanation: Shudder plus burnt fluid points to slip/wear; verify fluid, pressure, and data first.

options.label: A
options.body: Normal operation needing no checks

options.label: B
options.body: Belt/chain slip and wear from degraded fluid or low pressure — check fluid, pressures, and scan data before condemning the unit

options.label: C
options.body: A flat spot on a tire

options.label: D
options.body: Low windshield washer fluid

questions.prompt: What protects a CVT if the belt begins to slip excessively?
questions.explanation: The TCM raises clamping pressure and can limit torque/limp to protect the pulleys.

options.label: A
options.body: Nothing — slip has no effect

options.label: B
options.body: Control strategies raise clamping pressure and may limit engine torque / enter a limp mode to prevent pulley damage

options.label: C
options.body: The driver must select Park immediately in all cases

options.label: D
options.body: The pulleys lock together permanently

questions.prompt: The 'rubber band' feel drivers report in some CVTs is:
questions.explanation: RPM flare/hold while speed builds is normal CVT ratio behaviour, within limits.

options.label: A
options.body: A slipping accessory belt

options.label: B
options.body: Engine RPM rising and holding while vehicle speed catches up, because ratio changes separately from road speed

options.label: C
options.body: The tires stretching under load

options.label: D
options.body: A faulty accelerator cable in all cases

questions.prompt: Some CVTs offer simulated 'steps' in manual/sport mode. These are:
questions.explanation: Stepped feel is software — the pulleys jump between preset ratios.

options.label: A
options.body: Real additional fixed gears fitted inside

options.label: B
options.body: Programmed pulley ratio jumps that imitate stepped shifts for driver feel

options.label: C
options.body: Changes to the final drive gearing

options.label: D
options.body: Produced by the torque converter only

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a transfer case?
questions.explanation: The transfer case distributes drive to front and rear axles.

options.label: A
options.body: To boost engine power

options.label: B
options.body: To split drive between the front and rear axles on four-wheel-drive / all-wheel-drive vehicles

options.label: C
options.body: To replace the main gearbox

options.label: D
options.body: To operate the parking brake

questions.prompt: Where is the transfer case normally fitted?
questions.explanation: It sits after the transmission and feeds both propshafts.

options.label: A
options.body: In front of the engine

options.label: B
options.body: Behind (after) the main transmission, before the front and rear propshafts

options.label: C
options.body: Inside the fuel tank

options.label: D
options.body: On the steering column

questions.prompt: What does low range (4L) provide compared with high range (4H)?
questions.explanation: Low range adds a reduction gear for high torque at low speed.

options.label: A
options.body: Higher top speed

options.label: B
options.body: A deep extra reduction — much more wheel torque at lower speed for climbing, towing, and off-road work

options.label: C
options.body: No drive to the front axle

options.label: D
options.body: Automatic tire inflation

questions.prompt: Inside many transfer cases, drive to one output is carried by:
questions.explanation: Many transfer cases use a chain drive (some use gears) to the second output.

options.label: A
options.body: A timing belt

options.label: B
options.body: A wide chain (or gear drive) between the input and the second output shaft

options.label: C
options.body: A hydraulic motor only

options.label: D
options.body: The exhaust system

questions.prompt: Part-time 4WD with a locked centre (no centre differential action) should not be used on dry paved roads because:
questions.explanation: Locked front/rear speeds on high-grip surfaces cause wind-up and scrub in turns.

options.label: A
options.body: It uses too much fuel only

options.label: B
options.body: Front and rear axles are forced to turn at the same speed, causing driveline wind-up, tire scrub, and strain in turns

options.label: C
options.body: It disengages the brakes

options.label: D
options.body: It overheats the radio

questions.prompt: What is driveline wind-up (binding)?
questions.explanation: Wind-up is stored torsional load when locked axles travel different distances in a turn.

options.label: A
options.body: A loose propshaft bolt

options.label: B
options.body: Torsional stress built up when front and rear wheels are forced to rotate at different-path speeds with no centre differential to allow it

options.label: C
options.body: A worn wheel bearing noise

options.label: D
options.body: The transfer case oil foaming

questions.prompt: An electronically controlled transfer case changes range/mode using:
questions.explanation: Electronic cases use a shift motor and position feedback under module control.

options.label: A
options.body: The driver's hand on a lever in all modern cases

options.label: B
options.body: An electric shift motor/actuator commanded by a control module, often with position sensors to confirm the shift

options.label: C
options.body: Engine vacuum only

options.label: D
options.body: The ABS pump

questions.prompt: A transfer case will not shift into low range. A common requirement that must be met first is:
questions.explanation: Most systems require stop/near-stop and Neutral before a low-range shift.

options.label: A
options.body: Vehicle at motorway speed

options.label: B
options.body: Vehicle stopped or nearly stopped, transmission in Neutral, foot brake applied (per manufacturer procedure)

options.label: C
options.body: Headlights switched on

options.label: D
options.body: Fuel tank full

questions.prompt: Why is the specified transfer case fluid and level important?
questions.explanation: Correct fluid/level protects the chain, bearings, and any clutch pack inside.

options.label: A
options.body: It only affects the paint on the casing

options.label: B
options.body: The chain, bearings, clutches, and shift components rely on it; low or wrong fluid causes noise, poor shifting, and wear

options.label: C
options.body: Transfer cases are dry inside

options.label: D
options.body: Any fluid level is acceptable

questions.prompt: A vehicle with an active (on-demand) transfer case mainly drives one axle and engages the other when:
questions.explanation: On-demand systems apply an internal clutch to add the second axle when slip demands it.

options.label: A
options.body: The headlights are on

options.label: B
options.body: Wheel slip or driving conditions are detected and the module applies a clutch pack to send torque to the second axle

options.label: C
options.body: The driver opens a door

options.label: D
options.body: Engine temperature is low only

courses.title: Understanding Final Drives
moduleTitles: Drive Shaft Universal and Consistent Velocity Joint Operation

questions.prompt: The final drive performs two main jobs. They are:
questions.explanation: The final drive gives the last reduction and the differential splits drive/speed.

options.label: A
options.body: Cooling the engine and charging the battery

options.label: B
options.body: Providing the last gear reduction and, through the differential, turning drive through 90 degrees on a conventional rear axle while allowing wheels to turn at different speeds

options.label: C
options.body: Filtering the oil and pumping fuel

options.label: D
options.body: Locking both wheels permanently together

questions.prompt: A final drive ratio of 4.1:1 means:
questions.explanation: 4.1:1 = propshaft turns 4.1 times per wheel/ring-gear turn.

options.label: A
options.body: The wheels turn 4.1 times for each propshaft turn

options.label: B
options.body: The pinion/propshaft turns 4.1 times for each turn of the ring gear and wheels

options.label: C
options.body: Top speed is 4.1 mph

options.label: D
options.body: There are 4.1 gears in the axle

questions.prompt: Why does an open differential allow the driven wheels to turn at different speeds in a turn?
questions.explanation: Differential pinions walk between side gears to allow a speed difference.

options.label: A
options.body: It disconnects one wheel completely

options.label: B
options.body: Its planet pinions rotate on their pin, dividing speed between the side gears while still delivering drive

options.label: C
options.body: It locks the axles with a chain

options.label: D
options.body: It changes the final drive ratio

questions.prompt: Incorrect ring gear and pinion backlash / contact pattern after axle work will most likely cause:
questions.explanation: Wrong backlash/mesh gives noise on drive/coast and rapid wear.

options.label: A
options.body: Improved fuel economy

options.label: B
options.body: Whine or clonk on drive/coast and accelerated gear wear

options.label: C
options.body: The clutch to slip

options.label: D
options.body: Loss of steering assistance

questions.prompt: A limited slip differential (LSD) improves on an open differential by:
questions.explanation: An LSD biases torque toward the gripping wheel when slip begins.

options.label: A
options.body: Removing the need for axle oil

options.label: B
options.body: Transferring some torque to the wheel with grip when the other wheel starts to spin, instead of sending nearly all speed to the spinning wheel

options.label: C
options.body: Locking the steering in a straight line

options.label: D
options.body: Increasing tire tread depth

questions.prompt: In a clutch-pack LSD, the limiting action comes from:
questions.explanation: Clutch packs, loaded by ramps/preload, resist differential action.

options.label: A
options.body: Brake pads on the wheels

options.label: B
options.body: Friction clutch packs compressed as torque is applied (often with preload), resisting a speed difference between the wheels

options.label: C
options.body: Magnets in the axle tubes

options.label: D
options.body: The ABS module only

questions.prompt: A Torsen-type LSD gets its name and action from:
questions.explanation: Torsen = torque sensing; its worm gearing biases torque mechanically.

options.label: A
options.body: Torque sensing — worm-type gearing that biases torque to the slower, gripping wheel

options.label: B
options.body: Temperature sensing in the oil

options.label: C
options.body: A torsion bar in the suspension

options.label: D
options.body: Total lock at all times

questions.prompt: A single universal (Cardan) joint working at an angle produces:
questions.moduleTitle: Drive Shaft Universal and Consistent Velocity Joint Operation
questions.explanation: An angled UJ speeds and slows the output twice per turn; phasing/CVs cancel it.

options.label: A
options.body: Perfectly constant output speed

options.label: B
options.body: A twice-per-revolution speed fluctuation in the output shaft, which is why joints are phased/paired or CV joints are used

options.label: C
options.body: No movement at all

options.label: D
options.body: Only noise, with no speed change

questions.prompt: A constant velocity (CV) joint differs from a simple UJ because it:
questions.moduleTitle: Drive Shaft Universal and Consistent Velocity Joint Operation
questions.explanation: CV joints keep output speed constant through steering/drive angles.

options.label: A
options.body: Cannot transmit drive at an angle

options.label: B
options.body: Transmits drive at a constant output speed even at an angle, as used on front-wheel-drive shafts

options.label: C
options.body: Only works in a straight line

options.label: D
options.body: Needs no grease or boot

questions.prompt: A clicking noise on full steering lock at low speed most likely indicates:
questions.moduleTitle: Drive Shaft Universal and Consistent Velocity Joint Operation
questions.explanation: Clicking on lock is the classic worn outer CV joint symptom, usually after boot failure.

options.label: A
options.body: A worn outer CV joint, often after a split boot let grease out and dirt/water in

options.label: B
options.body: Low engine oil

options.label: C
options.body: A slipping clutch

options.label: D
options.body: Worn brake pads
